$comment: OBRS-602. The declared partition of the Playwright suite. Enforced by scripts/check-e2e-lanes.mjs; explained in docs/e2e-lanes.md. A spec belongs to exactly one lane, and the lane says what the spec needs to be TRUE, not what it happens to run under today.

lanes.GATE: Hermetic. Intercepts every call it makes, so it needs no backend, no seeded data and no external service. This is the only lane that is a merge gate. Run: npm run e2e:gate
lanes.GATE-BLOCKED: Mocks all of its own API traffic but still boots with a session minted from live SIT by e2e/global-setup.ts -- as fragile as SIT despite needing nothing from it. EMPTY since OBRS-618 moved all four members into GATE via e2e/support/gate-admin-session.ts, and that is the intended steady state: a spec parked here should leave again, not settle.
lanes.SIT-LIVE: Deliberately hits the deployed SIT backend, per docs/adr/0001-admin-e2e-hits-real-sit-backend.md -- mocking would defeat the point, which is catching contract drift. Not a gate: shared mutable environment.
lanes.OWN-DB: Needs booking/report states that can only exist by construction, so it provisions its own database. See playwright.local.config.ts for the reasoning. Never runnable against SIT.
lanes.CAPTURE: Not a test. A screenshot/evidence script kept for reproducing card artefacts. Asserts little and is not expected to pass unattended.

specs.why: Single catch-all page.route on **/api/** fulfils every path; fake token seeded into localStorage. Nothing reaches the network.
Stubs its public calls and ABORTS unstubbed **/api/private/** traffic, failing by name if a call escapes (OBRS-535). Fake token, no real session.
Anonymous, fixture-driven. Became hermetic in OBRS-602 once GET /api/routes -- the call that resolves the slug for its own pickup-dropoff mock -- was stubbed too.
Anonymous; stubs stops, schedules and pickup-dropoff per describe. OBRS-602 added the GET /api/routes stub it had always left live.

Booking path on fixture stations and schedules. OBRS-602 added the GET /api/routes stub that /home's route-map issues. OBRS-856 split it in two: the walk is anonymous only as far as the review page (still open to guests on purpose), after which one test seeds a customer session in localStorage and the other asserts the guest is sent to /login. Still hermetic -- the seeded token is never validated by anything, since every API call is intercepted.

OBRS-854. Walks the counter-QR path end to end at a 390px phone viewport: logged out at /account, bounced through AuthGuard to /login, back to /account, dialog opened, translated confirm phrase typed, and DELETE /api/private/users/me asserted off the wire rather than by a success toast. Hermetic by construction -- it mints no session at all (arriving logged OUT is the scenario under test), one page.route fulfils every /api/** call including the login it performs, and accounts.google.com is aborted so /login's GIS script never leaves the box. It also seeds OBRS-867's obrs_analytics_consent_v1 to an ANSWERED value for most cases, because that bar is fixed to the bottom of the viewport and this page puts the close-account card last on purpose; the unanswered overlap is not hidden but pinned by its own test, which asks document.elementFromPoint what is really on top of the button rather than reasoning about z-index.

OBRS-867 AC-1, declared by OBRS-882 -- the card shipped this spec without a lanes.json entry, so it belonged to no lane and ran nowhere but by hand. OWN-DB rather than GATE for the same reason that lane exists: it asserts a state that can only exist by construction. It needs the `analytics-e2e` build configuration, the ONLY one carrying a real measurement ID, because it measures consent on the WIRE -- no request to googletagmanager/clarity/google-analytics before accept, and a MUST-CATCH case proving both really do fire after. Against any other build the IDs are blank, the loader no-ops, and every 'nothing was requested' assertion passes vacuously. It touches no database, but the lane's rule -- provisions the environment its premise needs, never runnable against SIT -- is the one that fits.

OBRS-867 AFTER evidence, declared by OBRS-882 (shipped undeclared alongside the spec above). Screenshots of the consent bar from the same build whose network behaviour the AC-1 suite asserts, plus a MEASURED contrast pair read off the painted pixels rather than out of variables.scss. Its purpose is a picture, so CAPTURE -- but note it is a harder-working capture than most in this lane: the contrast assertion can fail for a real reason.

OBRS-882. Two stubbed home-page calls (stops, schedules search) and nothing else, so it needs no backend by construction. It exists as the counterpart to e2e/support/analytics-consent.ts: with a settled PDPA answer now seeded lane-wide, this is the ONLY spec that still loads a page with OBRS-867's consent bar UP, and without it the seeding would be a mute rather than a repair. Asks document.elementFromPoint what is really on top of the usability FAB rather than reasoning about z-index -- the overlap is deliberate per the component's own SCSS, so it is pinned, not overturned. obrs-854-account-deeplink.spec.ts asks the same question of a different button at a phone viewport.

Every endpoint it touches is fulfilled from inline constants. OBRS-618 replaced its SIT-minted storageState with a synthetic in-browser session (e2e/support/gate-admin-session.ts); it now passes against no backend at all.

23 routes / 28 fulfils cover the backend entirely, and one test reads i18n JSON off disk -- no network. OBRS-618 swapped the SIT-minted storageState for the synthetic session and added an afterEach that fails by name if any authenticated call escapes its stubs.
Fully stubbed walk-in schedules and segments; the SIT-minted storageState was the only thing keeping it out, and OBRS-618 removed that dependency.

56 fulfilling routes. Its comment blamed a fake token for changing behaviour; OBRS-618 checked the code and nothing in src/app decodes a JWT -- AuthService treats it as an opaque string and reads roles from a separate localStorage key. The real cause was the OBRS-535 one: an unmocked authenticated call 401s and force-logs-out, which cannot happen in a lane with no backend. Promoted only after all 42 cases passed here.

OBRS-584. Sweeps eight customer pages in both themes and scores WCAG 1.4.3 (text) and 1.4.11 (control boundary) from getComputedStyle. Hermetic by construction: one page.route fulfils every /api/** call from inline fixtures, Maps is aborted, the session is a synthetic localStorage token and the booking flow is reached by dispatching the app's own NgRx actions rather than by driving the funnel. It needs a DEVELOPMENT build (window.ng, for the store seed), which is exactly what this lane's webServer serves.

OBRS-753. Asserts no component host in the review module is display:inline while wrapping block-level children, that a click at the confirm button's centre still hits the button, and that the fix moved no geometry at any of the four media-query widths. Hermetic on the same terms as customer-contrast-gate, whose fixtures and NgRx store seed it reuses (e2e/support/customer-pages.ts): no backend, no session minted anywhere, Maps aborted.

OBRS-767. Removes every dark-theme.scss declaration from the live CSSOM in turn and fails if nothing on the page changed. A rule that parses, matches its element and still loses to Angular's [_ngcontent] specificity is invisible to any source-reading check, and that shape had hidden the entire dark footer at 2.40:1 for the life of the feature. Reuses customer-pages.ts, so it is hermetic on exactly the same terms as the contrast gate, plus /register and /how-to-book to reach dark-theme.scss sections 5 and 9.

OBRS-775. Widens OBRS-753's one-module check to every page this lane can reach hermetically -- nine customer pages, nine public/auth-entry routes, twenty-nine admin/staff/session-bound routes, 47 screens in all -- and fails on any display:inline custom-element host holding in-flow block children that is not named on its ALLOW list with a reason. OBRS-776 added the twelve admin/staff pages and a second half: it derives from the source tree which components render p-tabview/p-tabpanel/p-card/p-calendar and fails on any the sweep did not MOUNT, because a clean census cannot tell a page that is well-formed from a page nobody opened -- which is what a global rule in src/styles/ needs before it can be trusted. Hermetic on the same terms as the rest of the lane: it reuses e2e/support/customer-pages.ts for the customer group and stubs every /api/** call itself for the other two, aborts Maps, and mints no session anywhere. Needs a DEVELOPMENT build for the same reason customer-contrast-gate does (window.ng, for the NgRx store seed). OBRS-782 reached the last seven components OBRS-776 had excused by variant, by giving SweepPage a `fixture` (per-screen JSON answered ahead of the empty backend) alongside its `act`: NOT_SWEPT is down to app-parcel-trip-form, which expires by itself when its feature flag flips. Still hermetic -- a fixture is one more canned answer from the same page.route, not a backend. The five added screens turned up three malformed hosts nothing had ever measured.

The spec ADR-0001 was written for: create Vehicle / ScheduleSet / Schedules against the real backend so a malformed payload cannot pass. OBRS-617 added e2e/support/sit-sweep.ts, called in beforeAll (self-heal) and afterAll (leave zero) -- it no longer leaves TEST- litter behind on SIT.

OBRS-617 AC-4. Purely API-driven: seeds a TEST- route + ScheduleSet on the real backend, runs sweepSitTestLitter(), and asserts both are gone. MUST use its own config -- it has no page.goto, so it needs no webServer/globalSetup, and riding playwright.config.ts would drag the ng-serve build that a fresh worktree cannot compile (OBRS-536). Mutates SIT by design, self-cleaning.
Stubs the users list and the unlock PUT because SIT pre-dates the locked field, but the rest of the admin shell is served live.
Queries the SIT API directly and asserts the six seeded dropoff stops still carry placehold.co URLs -- by design it goes red when the Places backfill succeeds.
Zero mocks. Posts a real verify-email request and performs a real login, with a 60s allowance for Koyeb cold start.
Zero mocks and a real admin session across /staff and /admin shells; pure live-render coverage.
Deliberately leaves /api/routes* live and asserts the seeded SIT stop lists (19 pickup, first 'Nong chak') -- verified still accurate on 2026-07-21.
MUST use its own config: the defect is a CSS rule below 576px and the assertions are meaningless at the default 1280px, where it would pass while measuring nothing.
Needs five E2E-* bookings including already-rescheduled, cancelled and seat-collision states, and mutates them. On SIT those states can only be produced by running the spec, which spends them.

OBRS-732. Needs a booking that is `pending`, unexpired, unpaid and free of any in-flight payment -- five conditions PaymentService.validateBookingForPayment enforces and which the reschedule fixture deliberately does not satisfy (its design keeps `payments` out of it entirely). Provisions its own database through the OBRS-184 boot script with E2E_FIXTURE_SQL pointed at obrs-732-3ds-fixture.sql. NOT hermetic on purpose: it really charges api.omise.co in TEST mode and really walks Omise's hosted 3DS page, because 3-D Secure leaves our origin and returns through return_uri -- a mocked one would evidence nothing. Never a gate: it depends on a third party's uptime. (OBRS-735: this used to also cite an Actions minute ceiling -- false, this repo is PUBLIC and unmetered.) SCOPE BOUNDARY: it stops at /payment/result with a real chrg_ id, and deliberately does NOT assert fully_paid -- after 3DS the charge stays pending until OmiseWebhookService receives an INBOUND call from Omise, which cannot reach a laptop, and nothing else in the system reconciles it (the result page only polls, the endpoint only reads the database, no @Scheduled job covers it). Asserting settlement here would be permanently red and would read as a product defect.
Needs booking OBRS483-OPEN with a null seat from its SQL fixture, and a backend built from the OBRS-483 branch. The frontend alone is not sufficient.

OBRS-766. Every case here CONSUMES the booking it acts on -- cancelling is the thing under test -- so each seeds its own walk-in sale through the real API instead of depending on a booking a previous run already spent. Needs states SIT cannot be asked for: a CASH sale (to reach the OBRS-669 second-person step-up), a payment-less booking (to resolve MANUAL_REFUND_REQUIRED), and a booking departing inside the 2h window (produced by rewriting booking_schedules.departure_date_time, since the seeded cluster starts December 2026). Its globalSetup frees seat inventory first: one pass consumes 7+ of the 14 seats per vehicle type, and without the reset the third pass fails at seeding with BOOKING_ERROR_SEATS_INSUFFICIENT -- which reads exactly like a product regression and is not one. Never a gate: it mutates its own database and shells out to psql.

OBRS-766. The card's load-bearing case in one continuous flow: a SALESPERSON logs in, finds a walk-in booking they did NOT sell, sees the refund preview before committing, and cancels it under the second-person cash approval -- the proof that act-on-behalf (OBRS-661) and the cash step-up (OBRS-669) are reachable at all, since neither had a UI before this card. Shares the OWN-DB reasoning and globalSetup above. Also asserts the masked phone never appears raw in the DOM or in any response body, so it doubles as the anti-enumeration guard for GET /api/private/bookings/search.
Asserts exactly four seeded reports and a QA-SEED follow-up, then edits them irreversibly. Requires a fresh obrs433qa database.

specs.config: none -- run by hand against obrs564qa on :8080
specs.why: Calls http://localhost:8080 directly and writes the global booking cap to 45, resetting it in a separate test that a mid-suite failure skips. Must never point at a shared environment.

specs.config: none -- run by hand against obrs576qa on :8080
specs.why: Asserts hand-seeded synthetic history rows that no script in this repo creates, and appends new rows on every run. Provisions nothing itself.

specs.config: none -- no committed config runs it. It is hermetic and uses baseURL-relative navigation, so it needs only a `testMatch` pointing at it; run it with `npx playwright test --config=playwright.gate.config.ts` ONLY after temporarily adding it, which the lane gate will then reject. Adding it to the GATE lane for real is the clean fix if the capture is still wanted.
specs.why: Fully mocked and technically hermetic, but its purpose is producing the OBRS-296 before/after e-ticket screenshots, not asserting behaviour.
Screenshot script. Expects two servers started by hand on :4575 and :4576 -- one of them serving origin/dev for the BEFORE shot.

Screenshot script for the OBRS-702 before/after. Expects two servers started by hand on :4702 and :4703 -- :4702 serving a throwaway worktree at origin/dev 3eff9dc1 for the BEFORE shot. Hermetic otherwise (synthetic session, stubbed config reads), but its purpose is evidence, not a verdict.

Screenshot script for the OBRS-391 before/after. Expects two servers started by hand on :4391 and :4392 -- :4391 serving the main clone at origin/dev for the BEFORE shot. NOT hermetic on purpose: it stubs every /api/** call but reaches cdn.omise.co for real, because the claim being evidenced is that the card fields now render in a third-party iframe and a stubbed frame would prove nothing. environment.base.ts carries a test-mode publishable key, so no charge is possible.

OBRS-775's AC3 evidence, re-used by OBRS-776: the border box of EVERY element on all 39 pages of the host-box sweep (27 when OBRS-775 wrote this), at the four media-query widths, captured once with the `:host { display }` additions absent (OBRS775_PHASE=before) and once with them applied. The AFTER phase reads the baseline back and fails on any box that moved more than 0.5px, so it is an assertion rather than a screenshot -- but it is still a two-run, run-by-hand comparison, which is why it is not in GATE. Hermetic: it reuses the same e2e/support/host-boxes.ts fixtures the gate spec does, so no backend and no database.

Screenshot script for the OBRS-742 before/after. The ONLY capture here that needs a live stack: it logs into a real backend on :8080 over a disposable obrs742qa database and photographs six history rows written through OBRS-730's real owner-override endpoint, because the INSERT row (old_value NULL) this card fixes cannot be produced any other way -- OBRS-722's capture had to stub its rows precisely because that endpoint did not exist yet. BEFORE and AFTER are served one at a time on :4200, the dev profile's only allowed CORS origin, BEFORE from a throwaway detached worktree at origin/dev 1b5c852d. Evidence, not a verdict.

Screenshot script for the OBRS-722 before/after. Expects two servers started by hand on :4722 and :4723 -- :4722 serving a throwaway detached worktree at the then-current origin/dev (45c66cbd) for the BEFORE shot. Hermetic otherwise (synthetic session, one stubbed history page), but its purpose is evidence, not a verdict.
Hardcodes http://localhost:4575 for every navigation, bypassing baseURL, and depends on recent-route history existing for the seeded customer.

OBRS-769's evidence: every sighting of the two muted text tokens with the background it MEASURED under, on the contrast gate's own eight pages in both themes. The gate prints only what fails, and this card turned on what still PASSED -- #989ba4 was 2.78:1 on white at 39 sightings and 5.38:1 on the dark booking card at one, so a single repoint could not serve both. Hermetic (it reuses customer-pages.ts fixtures and MEASURE, so no backend), and it does assert its own population is non-empty, but its output is a census for a human to read rather than a verdict. Re-run it before changing $text-lightblack: npx playwright test --config=playwright.obrs769.config.ts

OBRS-769 before/after evidence. Two servers started by hand -- :4761 a throwaway detached worktree at origin/dev c1388c27 for the BEFORE shot, :4762 this one -- and run once per phase with OBRS769_PHASE. TWO separate clipped frames per phase rather than one composed sheet, because OBRS-811 composed four dropdown panels into a single image and a reviewer read it as a layout bug. Hermetic otherwise (customer-pages.ts fixtures), but its purpose is a picture, not a verdict.
